headline: We built Spark to help founders hire without the chaos.

headline: We built Spark because job seekers deserve a better system.
subline: You deserve to understand the system you are up against.
caption_linkedin:
Spark Careers was built on a simple observation: the hiring process was not designed with job seekers in mind.

Resumes get filtered by software before a human ever reads them. Applications disappear without a reply. Feedback is rare. The process is opaque by design, and job seekers are expected to keep trying without knowing why things are not working.

We built Spark to change that side of the equation.

Spark shows you how your resume scores against the ATS criteria for the roles you are applying to. It tells you what is being filtered out and why. It gives you a path forward instead of silence.

You deserve to know where you stand. That is what this platform is for.

headline: A clean pipeline moves candidates faster than any job post.
subline: Slow decisions come from poor tracking, not a talent shortage.
caption_linkedin:
Trade Secret No. 25 for founder-led hiring: a messy candidate pipeline costs you more than a long time-to-hire.

Here is what that looks like in practice. You post a job. Applications come in. You review a few, flag some for later, and then three client calls happen and two weeks pass. By the time you come back to the pile, your top candidate has already accepted another offer.

The bottleneck was not the talent. It was the tracking.

Founders who hire well tend to do one thing consistently: they move fast on the candidates they like. Not recklessly, but decisively. That requires knowing at any moment where every person in the pipeline stands.

This is harder than it sounds when your ATS is a spreadsheet and your notes are scattered across three different email threads.

A clean pipeline, even a simple one, changes the math. When you can see who is at what stage with one glance, you make faster decisions. Faster decisions mean less candidate drop-off. Less candidate drop-off means better hires.

You do not need a sophisticated system to get there. You need a consistent one.

Start with this: at the end of every day you do any hiring work, update the status of every candidate you touched. It takes five minutes and it compounds quickly.

If you want a tool that makes this automatic, Spark Enterprise was built for exactly this.

headline: Plain text gets further than a formatted resume every time.
caption_facebook:
Trade Secret No. 25 for job seekers: most ATS systems do not read formatting. They read plain text.

If your resume has tables, text boxes, columns, or graphic design elements, there is a good chance the ATS is reading scrambled output and scoring your application poorly, even if your experience is a strong match for the role.

The safest version of your resume for online applications is a clean, single-column, plain-text document. Save the designed version for interviews and networking conversations.

Spark can scan your resume and show you exactly how an ATS reads it.

https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w25-tue-b2c
caption_instagram:
ATS systems do not read your resume the way a recruiter does. Here is what that means for your job search.

Most online application portals use software to screen resumes before a human reviews them. That software reads plain text. It does not read tables, columns, or text boxes.

If your resume uses those design elements, the ATS may be reading scrambled output and ranking you lower than your experience deserves.

The simplest fix: use a clean, single-column format for online applications. Save the designed version for when you are in front of the hiring manager.

Spark can show you exactly how your resume looks to an ATS before you submit.
